title: Slack-threaded runbook editor with inline trace patching and one-click remediation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
We frequently see noisy Slack incident threads where responders paste large trace snippets and ad-hoc steps; that creates cognitive overhead and hinders fast remediation. The goal of this ticket is to build an in-Slack threaded runbook editor that lets responders assemble a compact runbook from telemetry fragments, apply inline trace 'patches' (trim/annotate spans), and publish a one-click remediation action that can trigger a safe runbook play (rollback, config toggle, scale-up).

Goals / Success metrics:
- Reduce average mean-time-to-ack (MTTA) for P1 incidents related to serving runtime by 20% in first 8 weeks.
- 80% of incidents created via PD->Slack workflow to have a structured runbook link included within 10 minutes.
- Runbook actions executed with confirmation modal; track success/failure and attach outcome to postmortem.

Design notes / user flow:
1) PD alert triggers Slack incident thread via existing ops bridge. A small 'Runbook' button appears in the thread (Slack message action).
2) Clicking opens an editor UI embedded in Slack (modal) that pre-populates candidate steps assembled from searchable playbooks and recent trace snippets related to the incident (trace selection via trace IDs / span fingerprint).
3) Inline trace patching: responders can trim long traces to 1-3 critical spans, add annotations, and tag spans with suspected root-cause labels. The UI will persist both original and edited snippet.
4) One-click remediation: authoring a runbook step can include an optional executable action (k8s scale, runtime toggle, traffic weight change). Actions go through RBAC check and present a confirmation modal.
5) Telemetry: every edit and execution logs to observability pipeline (events + trace linkage) and creates an evidence bundle attached to the PD incident.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Spike (1): Slack modal prototype + basic editor with text + trace snippet rendering (ETA 2 weeks).
- Integration (2): Trace selector service that queries tracing backend by trace IDs / span fingerprints; produce compact snippets and metadata (ETA 3 weeks).
- RBAC + action runner (3): Secure action execution via internal runbook-runner service with audit logs and dry-run mode (ETA 3 weeks).
- UX polish + telemetry (4): Attach evidence bundle to PD, add dashboards showing runbook executions and outcomes (ETA 2 weeks).

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Storing edited trace snippets: persist full original vs. only edited view? We will persist both but redact PII by default. Need legal sign-off on retention window.
- Action sandboxing: start with a whitelist of safe remediation actions (scale, feature flag toggle) and expand post-release.
- Slack modal limits: heavy editing UIs are constrained; we may surface a link to a lightweight editor web app for complex edits.

QA and rollout plan:
- Canary: enable for internal ops team only for 2 weeks; record metrics and iterate.
- Beta: opt-in for 3 product teams.
- Full rollout: enable by default for accounts with dedicated PD integration.

Observability & dashboards:
- New dashboard: "Runbook Editor Adoption" (route: console/ops/runbook-adoption) showing creation rate, execution success rate, and MTTR delta.
- Error dashboard: track failed action attempts, RBAC denies, and trace patch rejections.

- 2026-03-02 (Marcus L): Hooked up trace selector to tracing API; discovered queries are slow for large traces — adding sample-based indexing.
- 2026-03-08 (Security): flagged retention policy for edited snippets; legal loop required. Created follow-up: ENG-678100 (retention-policy).
- 2026-03-10 (Marcus L): Implemented RBAC deny flow and added audit event emission to telemetry pipeline. Local E2E test for safe action succeeded in dry-run mode.

Review requests / PRs:
- @sophia.ng please review RBAC integration design (PR: ops-infra#431)
- @ryan.tu requested to validate PD attachment format for automatic postmortem seeding

Next steps:
- Finish web-based editor fallback surface for complex edits (spike: 3d)
- Work with Legal on retention policy (ENG-678100) and include redaction step in pipeline
- Add runbook action whitelist and governance dashboard before beta enablement

Executive summary for on-call leads: This feature reduces cognitive overhead by turning ad-hoc Slack threads into structured, executable runbooks with evidence attached. It bridges tracing telemetry with actionable remediation, preserving audit trails and enabling faster, safer incident recovery.
